set_title: Early pregnancy signs: Chadwick sign, Goodell sign, Hegar sign, Linea nigra and Melasma (chloasma)
stem: A 27-year-old woman with 7 weeks of amenorrhea has a positive urine hCG. On speculum examination, the cervix and vaginal walls look blue-violet.
oneliner: 27F, 7 weeks amenorrhea + blue-violet cervix and vagina on speculum → ?

whyNot.A: Goodell is cervical softening on palpation; she has a **bluish color on speculum exam**
whyNot.B: Hegar is isthmus softening on bimanual exam; her finding is **bluish discoloration**
whyNot.D: Linea nigra is an abdominal line; her finding is on the **cervix and vagina**
whyNot.E: Melasma is brown facial patches; hers is **blue-violet cervix**

why: Bluish discoloration of the cervix and vagina is the Chadwick sign, caused by pelvic venous congestion in early pregnancy.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Dark line from pubis to umbilicus

idea.rule: Blue cervix and vagina in early pregnancy = Chadwick sign.

set_title: Early pregnancy signs: Chadwick sign, Goodell sign, Hegar sign, Linea nigra and Melasma (chloasma)
stem: At 8 weeks of gestation, bimanual examination of a 25-year-old woman finds the lower uterine segment above the cervix so soft that the examiner's fingers nearly meet.
oneliner: 25F, 8 weeks pregnant + very soft lower uterine segment on bimanual exam → ?

whyNot.A: Chadwick is a bluish color on speculum exam; hers is **palpated softening**
whyNot.B: Goodell is cervical softening; her softening is **above the cervix in the isthmus**
whyNot.C: Linea nigra is a pigment line; her finding is **softening on palpation**
whyNot.E: Melasma is facial pigmentation; her finding is **uterine softening**

why: Softening of the uterine isthmus is the Hegar sign, appearing at about 6-12 weeks of pregnancy.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Dark line from pubis to umbilicus

idea.rule: Soft lower uterine segment on bimanual exam = Hegar sign.
also: Isthmus lies between cervix and corpus

set_title: Early pregnancy signs: Chadwick sign, Goodell sign, Hegar sign, Linea nigra and Melasma (chloasma)
stem: On bimanual exam, the cervix of a 24-year-old at 5 weeks of gestation feels soft like lips rather than firm like the tip of the nose.
oneliner: 24F, 5 weeks pregnant + cervix soft like lips → ?

whyNot.A: Cervical insufficiency causes painless dilation in the second trimester; her cervix is **only soft**
whyNot.B: Chronic cervicitis causes discharge and friability; she has **early pregnancy**
whyNot.D: Neoplasia is not detected by softening; hers is **early pregnancy**
whyNot.E: Estrogen deficiency firms the cervix; she is **pregnant with high estrogen**

why: A softened cervix in early pregnancy is the Goodell sign, due to increased vascularity and edema of the cervical stroma.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Dark line from pubis to umbilicus

idea.rule: Soft cervix in early pregnancy = Goodell; vascularity and edema.

set_title: Early pregnancy signs: Chadwick sign, Goodell sign, Hegar sign, Linea nigra and Melasma (chloasma)
stem: A 29-year-old woman taking oral contraceptive pills has symmetric blotchy brown patches on her cheeks and forehead that darken with sun exposure.
oneliner: 29F, on oral contraceptives + symmetric brown facial patches worse with sun → ?

whyNot.A: Autoimmune melanocyte loss causes white patches; hers are **brown**
whyNot.B: Iron deposition gives bronze skin in hemochromatosis; hers are **brown facial patches**
whyNot.C: A photosensitizing reaction causes erythema; she has **hyperpigmentation**
whyNot.D: Mast cell infiltration causes pruritic urticarial lesions; hers are **flat brown patches**

why: Melasma is brown facial hyperpigmentation driven by estrogen and progesterone stimulating melanocytes, worsened by sunlight; pregnancy and oral contraceptives are triggers.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Dark line from pubis to umbilicus

idea.rule: Brown facial patches with hormones = estrogen-driven melanocyte activity.
also: Also called the mask of pregnancy

set_title: Scrotal signs: Absent cremasteric reflex, Prehn sign, Blue dot sign, Bag of worms, Transillumination and High-riding horizontal testis
stem: A 15-year-old boy woke 3 hours ago with severe right scrotal pain and vomiting. The right testis is swollen and exquisitely tender. Stroking the right inner thigh does not elevate the testis; the left side responds normally.
oneliner: 15M, acute scrotal pain + vomiting + thigh stroke does not lift testis → ?

whyNot.B: Prehn sign is pain relief on elevation, not **failure of the testis to rise**
whyNot.C: Blue dot sign is a visible blue nodule; this exam shows **no thigh-stroke response**
whyNot.D: Bag of worms is a soft painless mass, not **acute severe pain**
whyNot.E: High-riding testis describes testis position; this exam tests a **thigh-stroke reflex**

why: **Failure of the testis to rise when the inner thigh is stroked** is an absent cremasteric reflex, suggesting testicular torsion in a boy with acute scrotal pain.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Thigh stroke fails to lift testis
Tender blue spot at upper testis
Soft scrotal mass, bigger when standing
Testis lies high with transverse axis

idea.rule: Acute scrotal pain + absent cremasteric reflex = torsion until proven otherwise.

set_title: Scrotal signs: Absent cremasteric reflex, Prehn sign, Blue dot sign, Bag of worms, Transillumination and High-riding horizontal testis
stem: A 28-year-old man has a dull ache in the left scrotum and has been unable to conceive for 2 years. Standing or straining produces a soft, nontender, rope-like mass above the left testis that shrinks when he lies down.
oneliner: 28M, infertility + left dull scrotal ache + rope-like mass, worse standing → ?

whyNot.A: Absent cremasteric reflex marks torsion with acute pain; his ache is **dull and chronic**
whyNot.B: Prehn sign is epididymitis pain easing on elevation; his mass is **nontender**
whyNot.C: Blue dot sign is a small tender nodule, not a **rope-like mass**
whyNot.D: Transillumination shows a glowing fluid mass, not a **rope-like mass**

why: A **rope-like scrotal mass that enlarges on standing** is a varicocele, a bag of worms; it is left-sided because the left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Thigh stroke fails to lift testis
Tender blue spot at upper testis
Soft scrotal mass, bigger when standing
Testis lies high with transverse axis

idea.rule: Left rope-like scrotal mass, worse standing = varicocele (bag of worms), infertility.
also: Sudden varicocele in older man: renal mass

set_title: Scrotal signs: Absent cremasteric reflex, Prehn sign, Blue dot sign, Bag of worms, Transillumination and High-riding horizontal testis
stem: A 5-month-old boy has a painless left scrotal swelling that is larger at the end of the day and smaller in the morning. A penlight placed behind the scrotum makes the swelling glow uniformly.
oneliner: 5-month-old M, painless scrotal swelling, larger by evening, glows with penlight → ?
ask: Which diagnosis best explains this finding?

whyNot.A: Varicocele is a rope-like mass that does not glow; his **glows**
whyNot.C: A solid tumor blocks light; his swelling **glows**
whyNot.D: Epididymitis is painful and does not **glow with a penlight**
whyNot.E: Torsion is acutely painful; his swelling is **painless**

why: A painless scrotal swelling that **glows with a penlight** is a hydrocele, fluid in the tunica vaginalis, here from a patent processus vaginalis.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Thigh stroke fails to lift testis
Tender blue spot at upper testis
Soft scrotal mass, bigger when standing
Testis lies high with transverse axis

idea.rule: Painless scrotal swelling that transilluminates = hydrocele; solid masses block light.
